title: Vice-President graces 42nd Annual Day celebrations of Nellai Nadar Matriculation Higher Secondary School in Chennai
subtitle:
Preserving Tamil language,culture and identity goes hand in hand with strengthening the nation: Vice-President

Research and innovation will shape the future; students must prepare themselves for it: Vice-President

Education must go beyond academic excellence to build responsible and compassionate citizens: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 NOV 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today addressed the 42nd Annual Day celebrations of Nellai Nadar Matriculation Higher Secondary School at Kottivakkam, Chennai, the Vice-President paid rich tributes to K.Kamaraj, recalling his selfless leadership, simplicity and commitment to public welfare.
He said that as long as the legacy of the great leader K. Kamaraj lives in Tamil soil, no force in the world can erase the spirit of nationalism from Tamil Nadu.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, graced the 42nd Annual Day celebrations of Nellai Nadar Matriculation Higher Secondary School at Kottivakkam, Chennai, today.

Highlighting the importance of scientific temper, research and responsible use of AI, he appreciated the school’s Atal Tinkering Labs for nurturing young innovators.

He called upon students to dream big, work hard and combine academic excellence with strong values, discipline and a spirit of service to the nation.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
November 21, 2026
He said that Kamaraj’s achievements in infrastructure and education remain unparalleled. Recalling the construction of several major dams during his tenure, he observed that the foundation laid by Kamaraj had been instrumental in making Tamil Nadu a state admired for its educational achievements and human resources. He described Kamaraj as a leader who never considered electoral gains or personal interests, but always placed public welfare above everything else.
Recalling Kamaraj’s contribution to the expansion of the school midday meal programme, the Vice-President said it reflected his commitment to ensuring that children from disadvantaged backgrounds had access to both education and nutrition.
Appreciating the Nellai Thoothukudi Nadar Mahamai Paripalana Sangam for its contribution to education, Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan said that the school, established in 1985 with just 85 students and seven teachers, had grown into an institution serving around 3,500 students with nearly 200 teachers and staff. He said this growth represented the fulfilment of the aspirations of thousands of families, particularly those from economically and socially disadvantaged backgrounds.
Emphasising that education must go beyond academic performance, he said schools must nurture students with strong values, compassion and a sense of social responsibility.
Referring to the Atal Tinkering Lab at the school, the Vice-President encouraged students to develop scientific temper, research aptitude and innovative thinking. He said India was making significant strides in research and development, and called upon students to prepare themselves to excel in research, innovation and new discoveries.
Highlighting the National Education Policy 2020, introduced under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he said it emphasised holistic development, mother-tongue education, experiential learning, vocational skills, research and innovation. He stressed the need to move beyond rote learning towards conceptual understanding and creative thinking.
The Vice-President also emphasised that scientific and technological progress must remain rooted in India’s cultural heritage and human values. He said that the preservation of Tamil language, culture and heritage was intrinsically linked to the strength of the nation. “If Tamil culture, the Tamil people and the Tamil language are to be protected, Bharat must remain strong,” he said.
Referring to India’s vision of becoming a developed nation by 2047, Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan called upon students to contribute to the nation’s progress through knowledge, innovation and dedication. He urged them to dream big, uphold integrity and achieve their goals through hard work and perseverance, without resorting to shortcuts.
During the occasion, the Vice-President inaugurated the Sports Auditorium and the Men’s Hostel of Nellai Nadar Engineering College.
The Vice-President also paid floral tributes to the statues of Thiruvalluvar and Thiru K. Kamaraj at Nellai Nadar Matriculation Higher Secondary School.

title: Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addresses 23rd Convocation of Symbiosis International University in Pune
subtitle:
India now has over 1,400 universities, up from 760 in 2014-15: Vice President

Education must become a bridge between nations, cultures and communities: Vice President

India emerging as a global knowledge hub through international education partnerships: Vice President

Over 80,000 professionals from Global South benefit from ITEC training since 2014: Vice President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 NOV 2026 2:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed the 23rd Convocation Ceremony of Symbiosis International (Deemed University) in Pune, Maharashtra, as the Chief Guest.
Vice President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the 23rd Convocation of Symbiosis International (Deemed University) in Pune, today as the Chief Guest.

Congratulating the graduates, he appreciated the truly global character of the University, with over 3,000 international students from 85 countries. Highlighting the University’s role in promoting international understanding, he said education must serve as a bridge between nations, cultures and communities, reflecting India’s ethos of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam - The World is One Family.

Governor of Maharashtra Shri Jishnu Dev Varma; Maharashtra Higher Education Minister Shri Chandrakant Patil; Chancellor Dr. Vidya Yeravdekar; Vice Chancellor Dr. Ramakrishnan Raman; and other dignitaries were present.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
November 21, 2026
Describing Symbiosis as a symbol of India’s commitment to international understanding, academic excellence and inclusive education, he said, “Its very name represents coexistence, mutual respect and the enrichment that comes from bringing different cultures and ideas together.” Referring to India’s civilisational ethos of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, he observed, “At a time when the world faces complex challenges, education must become a bridge between nations, cultures and communities.”
Appreciating Symbiosis’s international expansion, he noted that the University had established its first international branch campus in Dubai in 2024. He said such initiatives strengthened educational ties between India and the UAE and enhanced India’s presence in global higher education.
The Vice President noted that Symbiosis had over 62,000 students during the academic year 2025-26, including more than 29,000 women from across India. With over 3,000 international students from 85 countries, he said, the University reflects a strong commitment to inclusive and international education.
Highlighting women’s growing achievements in higher education, he said that during his visits to convocations across the country, he had consistently witnessed more women receiving degrees and medals than men. “To me, this is a visible sign of the growing strength of Nari Shakti. This is real women empowerment,” he said. He also appreciated the establishment of Symbiosis Medical College for Women as an important step towards expanding opportunities for women in medical education.
The Vice President said that India was progressing towards the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He highlighted the significant expansion of higher education over the last twelve years, stating that the number of universities had increased from 760 in 2014-15 to over 1,400 today. He noted that the number of IITs had grown from 16 to 23, IIMs from 13 to 22, and AIIMS institutions from 8 to 23. He further stated that higher education enrolment had increased from 3.4 crore in 2014-15 to more than 4.5 crore students.
Emphasising India’s role as a responsible global partner, the Vice President highlighted the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) Programme, which benefits professionals and officials from over 160 partner countries. Since 2014, he said, more than 80,000 professionals, including 30,000 women, from the Global South have benefited from ITEC training. “India firmly believes in sharing knowledge, skills and expertise with partner countries on the basis of mutual respect and equality,” he said.
He said initiatives such as UPI and India Stack demonstrated India’s growing contribution to global digital public infrastructure, financial inclusion and good governance. He added that the international campus of IIT Madras in Zanzibar, Tanzania, was another example of India’s expanding educational and technological partnership with Africa.
Recalling India’s G20 Presidency in 2023, the Vice President highlighted the African Union’s admission as a permanent member of the G20, describing it as an important step towards strengthening Africa’s representation in global decision-making.
Referring to rapid technological changes driven by artificial intelligence, digital technology, renewable energy and scientific innovation, the Vice President urged graduates to embrace lifelong learning. “Your degrees are valuable foundations, but lifelong learning will be your greatest asset,” he said.
Urging students to pursue excellence with integrity, he said, “Professional success is important, but character and ethical conduct are what create lasting respect.” He called upon graduates to contribute to nation-building through entrepreneurship, research, public service, industry and social innovation.
“Nation-building is not the responsibility of governments alone. It is a collective mission involving citizens, educational institutions, businesses and communities,” he said.
Expressing confidence in the graduating class of 2026, he said that young professionals would play an important role in India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047. He urged them to uphold the values of Symbiosis, contribute to society and bring pride to their families and institution.
He also urged students to say “No to Drugs.”

title: English rendering of PM's address during participation in Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 NOV 2026 9:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Uttar Pradesh's energetic Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath ji, my senior colleague in the Union Cabinet and representative from this very parliamentary constituency Shri Rajnath Singh ji, Shri Jayant Chaudhary ji, my colleague in Parliament Pankaj Chaudhary ji, Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya ji and Brajesh Pathak ji, other public representatives, and my young friends,
I am happy that our friend Jayant Chaudhary ji chose Lucknow for such a major skill development programme. You have already applauded, but I have not yet told you why I am happy. I am happy because, as a Member of Parliament from Uttar Pradesh, it is a matter of pride and good fortune for me that today I have the opportunity to welcome my young friends who have come here from across the country.
Friends,
Today, you have crossed an important milestone in your lives. You are now about to become directly connected with the process of nation-building. And today is a very important day for me as well. This morning, I left Delhi and went to Bengal, and my first programme of the day was at an IIT. The country's first IIT was established at Kharagpur, and it was celebrating its 75th anniversary. With the same energy, the same dreams, the same hopes and aspirations with which I went to meet the IIT students, I have come to meet the ITI students with equal enthusiasm and excitement. Whether it is an IIT or an ITI, for me they are equally the treasures of my country, the strength of my nation, and the future of India. The skills and expertise that you have gained while studying at ITIs are now a major source of energy for a Viksit Bharat. This Viksit Bharat will be built by your hands and by your skills. Every nation progresses through the skills of its youth, and our country has always respected skill and craftsmanship. Just look at Lucknow itself. How much Chikan embroidery work is done here. For a long time, India was known across the world through such skills. Fine muslin, the silk of Banaras and Kanchipuram, the Pashmina of Kashmir, our cotton fabrics, Kalamkari, the steel used to create some of the world's finest swords, bronze and Panchdhatu sculptures, and hundreds of countless such crafts. No one person could probably list them all together. These were once the pillars of our society.
Friends,
Earlier, our social system itself was built around skills. My birth took place in Gujarat, and I would like to share an experience from Gujarat. In Gujarat, there is a term called Vasvaya. This tradition meant that wherever a village was established, skilled people whose work sustained village life would also settle there. Only then could a village truly exist. These were people whose skills were so essential that village life could not even be imagined without them.
Friends,
Since ancient times, similar systems existed across every region of the country. But unfortunately, over time this system gradually lost its importance. When I was Chief Minister of Gujarat, a question once arose before me: how many types of skills are there without which our lives would become very difficult? I gave this assignment to my officers, and they came back with 30–35 categories. I told them not to approach it that way and suggested another method. I asked them to think from the moment a person wakes up in the morning until they go to sleep at night, and from birth until death. What kinds of services does an individual, a family, and society require? What services are absolutely essential? I told them to make a list using their own experience. Earlier, they had come back with only 30–35 categories. A week later, after thinking deeply about it, they returned with a list of nearly one thousand occupations. They realised that we need people who make bouquets, people who make toys, people who apply mehendi, and countless other service providers. These were the skills and craftsmanship that kept our society moving. I asked the officers to focus on this, and that eventually led to the creation of a modern skill development ecosystem in Gujarat.
Friends,
There is another reason behind the destruction of India’s skill ecosystem. When invaders came to our country, India was a golden civilisation, admired by the world and envied by many. What did those invaders do? Their first attack was on skill and craftsmanship. Many of you must have read in history how the thumbs of our master craftsmen were cut off whenever they created products of exceptional quality. Why? Because those invaders understood that India’s prosperity and greatness came from the skills in the hands of its people. They knew that if they destroyed those skills, they would weaken India itself. Later, the British came. They were more sophisticated in their methods. Through Macaulay’s education system, they imposed a model in which our skill-based traditions were reduced to producing clerks on paper. An entire system emerged that focused on producing clerks. The British destroyed India’s skills and advanced their own industries. They took our resources and expanded their manufacturing. Over time, becoming a paper-based clerk came to be regarded as prestigious. Even today, if a child joins an ITI, many parents do not proudly tell friends and relatives. They hide it. They feel embarrassed because the child is not going to a university or college. The child is wearing blue overalls and working with his or her hands. This mindset developed over time. I have resolved to change it. The respect given to IIT graduates should equally be given to my ITI students. Even in the largest company, there may be only two or three people walking around with degrees and certificates, but the company runs only because there are 200 to 300 ITI-trained workers supporting it.
And therefore, friends,
There is a great need for a psychological transformation in our social life. I congratulate Jayant Chaudhary ji and all the officers associated with this initiative. I was observing the sons and daughters who came to receive their certificates today. I saw their style and their attire. Convocations at universities do not have the kind of pride and dignity that I see among my ITI students. This confidence, this pride, is something special. The Prime Minister of India has come running from a programme in Bengal to stand here in Lucknow and proudly present certificates to ITI students.
Friends,
This was a colonial mindset from which the country never fully emerged, even after Independence. After Independence too, clerical jobs continued to be prioritised and skills gradually fell behind. Once, I read a book by Dada Dharmadhikari ji. A postgraduate youth came to him looking for a job and asked him to help find one. Dada Dharmadhikari asked him, “What do you know how to do?” The man replied, “I am a postgraduate.” Dada ji asked again, “But what can you actually do?” The young man said, “I have a gold medal. I have certificates. I am a postgraduate.” Dada ji asked again, “Can you drive a vehicle?” “No.” “Can you cook food?” “No.” Then what can you do? The young man kept repeating that he was a postgraduate. There was a period when paper certificates alone carried value. But times are changing, and today I want to tell you something. You must have seen discussions today in the media and on social media. People are saying that in 2023 I had suggested in Parliament that people invest in Government of India PSUs and become prosperous. At that time people mocked me. But history has shown that those who invested benefited significantly. I said another thing a year ago. I requested the people of the country not to buy gold for a year unless absolutely necessary. I am happy because just as people once followed Lal Bahadur Shastri ji’s request to skip one meal for the nation, our citizens listened. Such is the character of this nation. An ordinary person like me requested that people buy less gold, and they did. Gold prices fell. Today people tell me that they followed my advice and saved money. Today I want to say one more thing. Write it down. Times are changing. The demand for people with skills and craftsmanship is going to grow beyond those carrying only paper certificates and wearing coats, trousers, and ties. Those who possess real skills will be in greater demand. Whenever I visit Saudi Arabia, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Qatar, or Kuwait, members of the royal families tell me one thing. They say that the magnificent modern cities seen there were built not merely with their money, but with the hard work and skills of Indian workers. The splendour of Dubai, the shining skyline of Abu Dhabi, and the development of Saudi Arabia are all results of the skill and labour of Indian craftsmen. Every royal family praises India's human talent. Today, governments around the world entering agreements with us repeatedly tell us that they need 90,000 people every year, or 150,000 people, or 100,000 people. The whole world is asking for Indian talent. And they are not asking for graduates coming out of universities alone; they are asking for people coming out of ITIs. Those who possess skill and expertise are seeing growing demand across the world. That is why I say, friends, the next twenty years... and I am not referring to the movie... the next twenty years belong to a Viksit Bharat.
Friends,
India in the 21st century can move forward only by honouring skills. Therefore, in recent years our government has taken several steps inspired by the spirit of Shramev Jayate. We began by creating a separate Ministry for Skill Development. Earlier, convocation ceremonies were held only for college and university graduates. People wore large caps and gowns. I said no. If there should be grand convocation ceremonies, they should also be for my ITI students. I see India's future in their fingers. I see India's strength in their skills. And when we formulated the New National Education Policy, we placed special emphasis on skill development.
Friends,
In today's modern age, a great deal is being said about AI. People say AI will do this and AI will do that. AI will take away one person's job and another person's livelihood. But understand this carefully. No one can take away the livelihood of a skilled person. During COVID, we saw how difficult conditions became. People were helpless. Those whose services society depended on returned to their villages out of fear of death. And then people realised that no matter how wealthy they were, they could not manage without skilled manpower. It was skilled workers who sustained many aspects of life during that period.
Friends,
When you learn a skill, you are not merely working with machines. You are making people's lives easier. You are increasing the strength of the nation. There was a time when India imported mobile phones. Today, the sons and daughters of India manufacture those phones, and Indian-made mobile phones are being sent to countries around the world. It is because of you that India's manufacturing capacity is increasing. That is why ITIs are receiving so much importance today. Since 2014, our government has established nearly 5,000 new ITIs within a decade. The number of students enrolled in ITIs has increased by more than five lakh. Among them, the number of girls has increased by more than two and a half times.
Friends,
Training quality, faculty, and infrastructure in ITIs have also been very important priorities for us. Earlier, the ITI network was lagging behind. The same old trades were being taught under the label of skill and vocational education. Today, more than 30 new-age trades are being taught in ITIs. As was mentioned by Gen Z representatives, courses now include aeronautical structures, AI assistants, cyber security assistants, drone technicians, green hydrogen technicians, industrial robotics, electric vehicles, animation and special effects, semiconductor technicians, and many more. All these courses have been introduced keeping current and future needs in mind. No matter how big a hospital may be, no matter how highly educated the doctors are, if there are no ITI-trained technicians to operate the machines, not a single patient can be cured. That is the strength you possess. I have come here to make you realise your strength. I have come to honour your capability. Because I know that ITIs are going to write a glorious chapter in the future.
And friends,
All this is being done not only for India's requirements, but also keeping the needs of the whole world in mind. Every day you hear that India is signing trade agreements with one country or discussing FTAs with another. All of this is creating new opportunities for young people like you.
Friends,
Our effort is to transform ITI curricula, upgrade machinery, ensure that trainers learn new technologies, and build direct connections between training and industry. That is why ₹60,000 crore is being invested through the PM Setu Scheme. This is going to benefit all of you young people significantly.
Friends,
As India grows rapidly, new opportunities are emerging for skilled workers. You heard earlier that 50 crore people have emerged from poverty in the last 12–13 years. This is a historic achievement. In my view, one of the greatest achievements of India after Independence is precisely these 50 crore people coming out of poverty. And the path to a Viksit Bharat passes through this achievement. The government provided facilities, empowered the poor, and gave them confidence that they could rise above poverty. In this grand campaign, lakhs and lakhs of opportunities were also created for skilled workers. When four crore homes were built for poor families, electricians and carpenters found work. When pipelines were laid and when electricity reached villages for the first time, it was young people like you who made those initiatives successful.
Friends,
Today, demand for different skills is increasing in many new sectors. Let me give you another example. A few months ago, when war began in West Asia, gas supplies were disrupted. Questions arose about LPG availability. Clouds of uncertainty appeared. Those who love spreading panic became excited. They began saying that gas would disappear, stoves would stop working, people would go hungry, and queues would form at petrol stations. You can look at old newspaper reports and see what all was predicted. But none of it happened. At the same time, when the Strait of Hormuz crisis emerged, we also could not simply sit idle. We had to act. The government decided that at least one lakh PNG gas connections should be provided every day in urban areas. We wanted to ensure that gas reached households through pipelines so that we could withstand any future disruptions. I personally reviewed the programme because my objective was one lakh connections per day. Whenever I held review meetings, however, the numbers were only fifteen thousand, twenty thousand, twenty-two thousand, twenty-three thousand. We were unable to reach one lakh. The government was ready to spend the money. Do you know what answer I received? Officials told me that they had done everything possible, but they could not find enough plumbers. There was a shortage of plumbers. Just look at your strength. The country was searching desperately for plumbers. This shows that if you have skills, you have employment opportunities. Today we need huge numbers of skilled workers in solar energy. A completely new sports economy is emerging in India. We need manufacturers of sports equipment and many other products connected to sports and fitness. In other words, opportunities for you are expanding as wide as the sky itself. Our youth must take full advantage of these opportunities.
Friends,
Today, India is moving towards becoming the Skill Capital of the world, and all of you are at the heart of that vision. I am not speaking only about India; I am speaking about the world, and I say this with confidence because of you. And I have good news for all young people and for Uttar Pradesh. Next year, in 2027, India will host the World Skills Asia competition. Young people from across Asia will come here. And this event will take place in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh. Youth from many countries will be hosted by Uttar Pradesh. I extend my advance best wishes to Uttar Pradesh for this as well.
Friends,
Today, Uttar Pradesh is driving the country's development. There was a time when opportunities for young people here were very limited. Under the leadership of Yogi ji, Maurya ji, Brajesh ji, Pankaj Chaudhary ji, and others, and through the double-engine government, this situation has changed completely. Today people of Uttar Pradesh proudly say that UP is an expressway state. UP has numerous international airports. Major universities are being established here. Tourism is flourishing. Large mobile manufacturing facilities are operating here. A semiconductor plant is being built in Uttar Pradesh. And the BrahMos missile, which has gained great attention through Operation Sindoor and has disrupted the sleep of our enemies, is also being manufactured in Uttar Pradesh. All these development activities are creating new opportunities for young people like you.
Friends,
We must also remember what Uttar Pradesh used to be like. A few days ago, I was in my parliamentary constituency, Kashi. During the inauguration of a factory there, a young woman told me that she now works until 11 at night and returns home safely by herself. This is not an ordinary thing. People of Uttar Pradesh understand what it once meant for a daughter to be outside after sunset. She told me that after finishing work at the factory at 11 p.m., she goes home alone. Under the leadership of Yogi ji, the BJP government has created this environment of safety. A feeling of security and confidence in prosperity is what will build a Viksit Bharat. Therefore, I tell every young person in the country that the whole sky lies before you. Dream big. Develop your skills. Put all your energy into achieving your dreams. And never feel that you are alone. Whenever you think you are alone, remember that I stand with you. With this confidence, as all of you move forward into a new phase of life, fulfil all the dreams of your parents. Dedicate whatever you have gained to strengthening society. You will progress, the nation will progress, and your families will be filled with pride. With this spirit, I congratulate all of you on this special occasion. Just now, I was watching on television the many young people gathered in ITIs across the country. I congratulate all of them and extend my very best wishes.
Repeat after me:
Bharat Mata Ki Jai!
Bharat Mata Ki Jai!
Bharat Mata Ki Jai!
Bharat Mata Ki Jai!
Thank you very much!

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates, lays foundation stones for, and dedicates to the nation development projects worth around Rs. 34,470 crore in Vaishali, Bihar
subtitle:
We are building a Bihar that is stronger, more prosperous and full of opportunities: PM

Built across Maa Ganga, the six-lane Dargah-Bidupur cable bridge has been dedicated to the people; As a tribute to respected Nitish Ji, this modern bridge has been named 'Nitish Setu': PM

We have prioritized enhancing the ease of living for crores of poor citizens and providing them with essential amenities: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 NOV 2026 5:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated, laid the foundation stones for, and dedicated to the nation development projects worth around Rs. 34,470 crore in Vaishali, Bihar. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, the Prime Minister noted that the great festival of public faith, Chhath, has just concluded, during which mothers and sisters observed the arduous Nirjala fast to pray for the welfare of their families, society, and the world. “Now, with the blessings of Chhathi Maiya, we are celebrating the festival of development here,” remarked Shri Modi.
Emphasizing that Bihar's development journey has advanced with the mantra of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’ by turning the strength of democracy into a medium for public welfare, the Prime Minister noted that Vaishali, the great land of democracy, was fittingly chosen to mark the completion of one year of the government's current term. Bowing to the soil of Vaishali and Bihar, he congratulated everyone involved in the milestone.
Recalling how Bihar chose a new path of hope and trust nearly three decades ago, transitioning to a new assurance of good governance under respected Nitish Kumar's long tenure as Chief Minister, which is now being carried forward by Samrat Choudhary with his blessings, the Prime Minister highlighted the inauguration and foundation stone laying of development projects worth thousands of crores, including the dedication of the six-lane Dargah-Bidupur cable bridge over Mother Ganga named
‘
Nitish Setu’ in honor of Nitish Kumar. Pointing out that the bridge reduces distance and difficulties between Patna and Vaishali while making it easier to transport crops, fruits, vegetables, milk, and curd to major markets, he underlined its social impact. “The youth here will have easier access to education, and the elderly to healthcare,” noted Shri Modi.
Highlighting the rapid expansion of a modern road network across Bihar, the Prime Minister noted the inauguration of the Aurangabad-Chordaha six-lane highway along with the laying of foundation stones for several other highway projects. “Hundreds of crores of rupees will be spent on these projects,” noted PM Modi.
Observing that alongside the road network, Bihar's energy and urban development landscape is transforming rapidly through major initiatives such as the construction of the Buxar Thermal Power Plant, the foundation stone laying of the transmission system for the Pirpainti Thermal Power Plant, and the solar energy plant at Phulwaria Dam, the Prime Minister contrasted the state's past with its present. “There was a time when electricity had not reached thousands of villages in Bihar; today Bihar is becoming a major center of power generation,” observed Shri Modi.
Noting that 100 modern PM e-Buses were flagged off today to make urban transport convenient, alongside the handover of keys to pucca houses to thousands of poor families under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, the Prime Minister welcomed the progress. “I congratulate the people of Bihar for all these development works,” remarked PM Modi.
Reflecting on Bihar's long journey of transformation, the Prime Minister noted that today the focus is on investment figures, action against criminals, and a healthy race for development across the state. “Be it North Bihar, Nalanda-Gayaji, Shahabad-Kaimur, or the capital Patna, a new saga of development is being written in every region,” observed Shri Modi.
Citing the past year's achievements under the present government as proof of Bihar's rapid progress, the Prime Minister listed investment agreements worth over two lakh crore rupees, the start of work on a 6,000 crore rupee steel project in Gayaji, a new sugarcane incentive policy to revive closed sugar mills including Motihari, an initiative to install 11,000 new tubewells to deliver water to every field for farmers, a historic decision ensuring 12 hours of electricity for irrigation, the opening of over 200 new degree colleges in one year, and approval for the Maa Sita Mahila Vishwavidyalaya for daughters. “This list of Bihar's development is so long that it cannot be enumerated from any stage; the development of Bihar can only be felt by coming here,” remarked PM Modi.
Stating that clear intent produces visible results, the Prime Minister noted that his government lifted 50 crore people out of poverty within 12 years. “This is the result of the government's willpower, and this is the result of the government's schemes for the welfare of the poor,” asserted Shri Modi.
Explaining that India is winning the battle against poverty by prioritizing ease of living and facilities for crores of underprivileged citizens through free foodgrains for 80 crore people, pucca houses providing a sense of security to crores of families, guaranteed free medical treatment relieving the burden of expensive healthcare, and toilets, electricity, and water ensuring a dignified life, the Prime Minister highlighted the resulting transformation. “Because of this, even in those who were poor, a self-confidence awakened, and they have moved forward by defeating poverty,” observed PM Modi.
Highlighting Bihar's major contribution to the anti-poverty campaign through the hard work of the current government, where Central schemes were implemented and delivered door-to-door by the state government, the Prime Minister noted that 43 lakh families in Bihar received pucca houses with 11 lakh more approved in August, nearly 75 lakh farmers received thousands of crores under PM Kisan Samman Nidhi, and support for Self Help Groups empowered 50 lakh rural women as Lakhpati Didis. “It is the result of such efforts that today crores of people of Bihar have come out of poverty, and the country too has reached this success,” noted Shri Modi.
Concluding his address by extending best wishes for Bihar's unprecedented development journey, the Prime Minister called for sustained momentum among all coalition partners. “Now we must neither stop nor tire, and we must all work together continuously to build a capable, prosperous, and self-reliant Bihar,” asserted PM Modi.

About three decades ago, Bihar chose a new path of hope and confidence. Bihar, which had suffered neglect and decline for decades, received a new assurance of good governance under the leadership of respected Nitish ji. In this sequence, development projects worth thousands of crores of rupees have been inaugurated and launched here today as well. It will also greatly help the youth in pursuing education and the elderly in accessing medical care.
Friends,
The network of modern roads in Bihar is also expanding rapidly. Today, the Aurangabad-Chordaha six-lane highway has been inaugurated.
Friends,
I am extremely grateful for your affection. I must now proceed to Uttar Pradesh for another programme. Your affection is upon my head and in my heart. I have very little time, so I must complete my remarks today. But I express my gratitude. Today, I was observing the young people present here, and it truly filled my heart with happiness. The youth of my country, the youth of my Bihar, understand completely the importance of development. That is why I can see such enthusiasm and energy among them.
Friends,
Today, foundation stones have also been laid for many highway projects. Hundreds of crores of rupees will be spent on these projects.
Friends,
Along with the road network, the picture of energy and urban development in Bihar is also changing rapidly today. In this direction, major projects such as the construction of the Buxar Thermal Power Plant, the foundation stone of the transmission system for the Pirpainti Thermal Power Plant, and the solar energy project at the Phulwaria Dam have also been undertaken. There was a time when electricity had not reached thousands of villages in Bihar. Today, that same Bihar is steadily becoming a major centre of power generation.
Brothers and sisters,
Today, 100 modern PM e-buses have also been flagged off to make urban transport more convenient. Along with this, under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, thousands of poor families have been handed the keys to their permanent homes. I congratulate the people of Bihar for all these development works.
Friends,
Our Bihar has travelled a long journey to reach where it is today. Just remember what conditions were like before the NDA came to power. In those days, discussions revolved around scams. But today, figures of investment flowing into Bihar are presented. Earlier, discussions centred on crime statistics. Today, discussions revolve around action against criminals. Under NDA governance, one can see competition in development. Whether it is North Bihar, Nalanda-Gaya, Shahabad-Kaimur, or the capital Patna, every region is writing a new chapter of development.
Friends,
The pace of Bihar’s development under the double-engine government can be seen from the work undertaken even in the past year. Just look at it. Under the NDA government, investment agreements worth more than ₹2 lakh crore have been signed in Bihar. Work is beginning on a steel project worth ₹6,000 crore in Gaya. A new sugarcane incentive policy has been introduced to revive closed sugar mills, including those in Motihari. An initiative has been launched to install 11,000 new tube wells to ensure water reaches every field. A historic decision has been taken to ensure 12 hours of electricity for irrigation. More than 200 new degree colleges have been started in a single year. Approval has been given for the establishment of the Maa Sita Women’s University for our daughters. The list of development initiatives in Bihar is so long that it cannot be fully recounted from a single platform. Bihar’s development can only truly be experienced by coming here.
Friends,
When work is done with honest intent, results become visible. In the country where the Congress kept raising slogans of removing poverty for decades, misleading the poor and gathering votes, within just twelve years we have brought 50 crore people out of poverty. This is the result of the government's determination. It is the outcome of the government's welfare schemes for the poor.
Friends,
The country is winning this battle against poverty because we prioritised making the lives of crores of poor people easier and providing them with essential facilities. We provided free food grains to 80 crore people. We gave crores of families permanent homes and a sense of security. By guaranteeing free treatment, we freed people from the burden of expensive healthcare. Through toilets, electricity, and water connections, we enabled crores upon crores of poor citizens to live with dignity. As a result, even the poorest among them developed self-confidence and moved forward after overcoming poverty.
Friends,
Bihar has made a major contribution to the campaign against poverty. In recent years, the double-engine government has worked here with full dedication. The central government designed the schemes, and the NDA government in the state implemented them. Welfare schemes were delivered to every household. Just look at Bihar. Forty-three lakh families have received permanent houses. In August alone, approval was granted for another eleven lakh houses. Thousands of crores of rupees under PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi have been transferred to the accounts of nearly 75 lakh farmers in Bihar. The support provided by the government to self-help groups has enabled 50 lakh rural women here to become Lakhpati Didis. It is the result of such efforts that crores of people in Bihar have come out of poverty, and the country as a whole has achieved this success.
Friends,
Now we neither have to stop nor tire. All NDA constituent parties must continue working together to build a strong, prosperous, and self-reliant Bihar. With this resolve, I once again extend my heartfelt best wishes to all of you for this remarkable journey of development. Thank you all very much!

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi  participates in Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur
subtitle:
There are no limits to what young minds can achieve: PM

Today, as we move forward with the goal of Viksit Bharat, IIT Kharagpur's 75 years of experience is going to play a very big role in the country's development and in the country's innovation profile: PM

Nations realize their true potential only when they break the boundaries of their thinking; Over the past few years, India has unequivocally declared, “Break the Limits, Unlock the Possibilities” : PM

When you move forward with the mindset of ‘Nation First’, it will undoubtedly open up new opportunities for you while immensely benefiting the nation: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 NOV 2026 1:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur in West Bengal. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, the Prime Minister noted that before him stood a talented, aspirational generation connected with India's past, present, and future, gathered to celebrate the institute's 75-year journey and honor its legacy. Highlighting the numerous milestones IIT Kharagpur has created over 75 years, an era in which India has seen sweeping transformations from bullock carts to bullet trains and from postal letters to social media messages, he emphasized that as the country's first IIT, the institute has played an important role in every phase of these changes. “I extend my heartiest congratulations to all students here, faculty members, the entire staff here, and all alumni of IIT Kharagpur,” remarked Shri Modi.
Recalling that certain memories of campus life stay with one forever, the Prime Minister expressed confidence that many alumni fondly remember discussions over tea at Chedi's even decades later, and noted that unlike hostels in other institutions, IIT Kharagpur has Halls of which every student is deeply proud. Referring to the recent Diwali celebrations, he shared that he had been told Diwali enthusiasm at IIT Kharagpur is unique, with its Illumination carrying a charm of its own made even more special by the competition among different halls. “Which hall won in this competition this time?” asked PM Modi.
Highlighting Bengal as the land where ideas gained strength and national movements were born, the Prime Minister pointed out that IIT Kharagpur stands on the very site of a former Detention Camp for freedom fighters that decades ago witnessed the indomitable courage of Indians who wanted self-rule and aspired to see India at the pinnacle. Observing that the same campus today prepares youth whose innovation and ideas are becoming the strength to make India Atmanirbhar, he contrasted the past aspiration for Self-Rule and dream of Freedom with today's resolve of Self-Reliance and opportunity to build the Future. “This very journey from aspiration to self-reliance is the real energy of building a Viksit Bharat,” asserted Shri Modi.
Tracing IIT Kharagpur's journey from its founding in a newly independent India, before even the first General Election had been held, a time when the nation needed engineers for its industry and infrastructure, the Prime Minister noted that as India's scientific capabilities grew, its graduates advanced the Space and Atomic Energy programs, and later strengthened India's software industry and led major global companies during the Information Technology era and global economy. Emphasizing that the institute has consistently stepped forward to fulfill its nation-building responsibility in every era and that its 75 years of experience will play a major role in the nation's development and innovation profile as India moves toward Viksit Bharat, he expressed full faith in the students. “I am confident that you will leave no stone unturned in fulfilling the dreams of today's Aspirational India,” affirmed PM Modi.
Explaining that one's capability is determined by the courage to challenge obstacles rather than how quickly one sits back satisfied, the Prime Minister noted that people often place limits on their own thinking, known as limiting beliefs, which restrict their dreams, their talent, and the capability of their country, leading them to decide for themselves what is possible and what is not. “We end up considering the limit of our thinking itself as the limit of the world,” observed Shri Modi.
Stating that nations too recognize their capabilities only when they break the limits of their thinking, as India has demonstrated in recent years.  “India said boldly: Break the Limits, Unlock the Possibilities,” asserted PM Modi.
the Prime Minister stated that over the past 12 years, the government changed that mindset by strengthening and empowering the poor and launching schemes for their Ease of Living, whose results are visible today. Citing the latest World Bank report stating that 50 crore people in India came out of poverty in just 12 to 13 years, he underlined the significance of the achievement. “This is not a small change; this is the result of that mindset which says: Break the Limits,” observed PM Modi.
Offering the Semiconductor Mission as another example, the Prime Minister noted that its launch was met with numerous questions asking what the need was when other countries had been making semiconductors for 50 years and what India could possibly achieve now. “Therefore, when I spoke of the Semiconductor Mission, it was said that now it is too late,” remarked Shri Modi.
Stating that he remained firmly resolved and questioned whether India should still sit with its hands folded just because there was a delay earlier, the Prime Minister recalled making a beginning by personally bringing officers together to draw up plans. He noted that within four years, numerous semiconductor facilities have started across the country, India has begun exporting chips, and former IIT Kharagpur students are leading and executing many of these facilities. “But think, if we had accepted that it has been done over there and why should we make semiconductors now, then nothing would have happened at all,” remarked PM Modi.
Citing the space sector as another strong example, the Prime Minister noted that India's space ecosystem was previously confined to ISRO, where entry was largely restricted and every launch or mission followed its own distinct system, leaving young talent outside the organization with few opportunities. Recalling how he told the ministry that young innovators must get an opportunity and opened India's space sector to its youth, he highlighted that IIT Kharagpur alumnus Pawan built Skyroot Aerospace to give India the pride of launching its first private rocket, alongside many space startups accelerating India's space program today and turning what once seemed impossible into reality. “I can say with pride that your alumni have made a very big contribution in making this impossible possible,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Emphasizing that the country has great expectations from the students as the coming two decades will be among the most productive years of their lives and the most decisive years of India's development, the Prime Minister noted that many of them will be in leadership positions by 2047, making their every success vital for the nation. He urged them to always ask themselves which national challenge they would like to contribute toward solving and to remember his mantra of Nation First. “When you move forward with this mindset, then certainly, this will bring new opportunities for you too and the country will also benefit greatly,” asserted PM Modi.
Commending their wonderful work over the past 75 years and urging them to move forward with the firm resolve to work hard and celebrate the institute's 100-year ceremonies in a Viksit Bharat, the Prime Minister concluded his remarks by invoking Swami Vivekananda's words, ‘Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached’.

V. Narendran ji of IIT Kharagpur, Shri Suman Chakravarti ji, students, alumni members, other distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen.
First of all, I seek your forgiveness because I was delayed in arriving. Due to the weather, I could not reach on time, and then we travelled by road, but even then there was a delay. You had to wait for me, and for the inconvenience caused to all of you, I sincerely apologise.
Friends,
At this Platinum Jubilee celebration of IIT Kharagpur, I see before me India’s past, India’s present, and India’s future, all connected together. A very talented and highly aspirational generation is present here. Today, all of us have gathered to celebrate the 75-year journey of this institution and to honour its legacy. In the 75 years since its establishment, IIT Kharagpur has created many milestones. And in these 75 years, India has witnessed change from bullock carts to bullet trains, from postal letters to social media messages. In every phase of these transformations, as the country’s first IIT, IIT Kharagpur has played an important role. On this occasion, I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all the students, faculty members, staff, and alumni of IIT Kharagpur.
Friends,
Some memories of life at IIT Kharagpur stay with you forever. I am sure that many alumni here must still fondly remember discussions over tea at Chedis even after decades. Other institutions have hostels, but here you have Halls. And I know how proud every student is of their Hall. Before coming here, I was shown photographs of Diwali, and all of you have just celebrated it. I have been told that Diwali at IIT Kharagpur has a special excitement of its own. The illumination here has its own unique charm, and the competition among different Halls makes it even more special. Which Hall won this year? Look at how proudly they are saying it. Congratulations to the winners. If the winners themselves do not clap, then who else will clap for them?
Friends,
This land of Bengal is the land where ideas found strength, where national movements were born. And this institution stands on a site that was once a detention camp for freedom fighters. Just imagine what those freedom fighters who were held here must have discussed throughout the day. What thoughts must have occupied their minds? Their lives, their thinking, and their activities from that period must still resonate in the atmosphere here like a mantra, inspiring all of you. Decades ago, these detention camps witnessed the indomitable spirit and courage of Indians who wanted self-rule and wanted to see India reach great heights. Today, on the same land, our IIT, transformed into a new and vibrant institution, is producing young people whose innovations and ideas are becoming the strength of an Atmanirbhar Bharat. This land, which once aspired for self-rule, now reflects a resolve for self-reliance. Then there was a dream of freedom; today there is an opportunity to build the future. This journey from aspiration to self-reliance is the true energy behind the making of a Developed India.
Friends,
When IIT Kharagpur began its journey, India had only recently become independent. The country had not even held its first general election. At that time, India needed engineers for its industries and infrastructure. As the nation’s scientific capabilities expanded, graduates from here contributed to our space and atomic energy programmes. Then came the age of information technology and new opportunities in the global economy. The young people who emerged from this institution strengthened India’s software industry and played important roles in leading major global companies. In every era, this institution has stepped forward and fulfilled its responsibility in nation-building. And today, when we are moving ahead with the goal of a Developed India, the experience accumulated by IIT Kharagpur over 75 years will play a major role in the country’s development and innovation profile. I am confident that you will leave no stone unturned in fulfilling the dreams of today’s Aspirational India.
Friends,
Our true capability is determined by how courageously we challenge challenges. People often ask me about challenges. I tell them that it is in my nature that I cannot remain without challenging a challenge.
Friends,
The question is whether we challenge challenges or whether we become satisfied too quickly and sit down. Often, some people place limits on their own thinking. They define boundaries for themselves. This is what is called limiting beliefs. And what are limiting beliefs? Limiting beliefs are limiting your dreams. Limiting beliefs are limiting your talent. Limiting beliefs are limiting the capabilities of your country. We ourselves decide what is possible and what is not. Most people begin with, “No, this cannot happen.” Those who live with such dead thinking cannot truly live life, my friends. We end up treating the limits of our thinking as the limits of our world.
Friends,
Nations also recognise their capabilities only when they break the limits of their thinking. And India has demonstrated exactly this in recent years. India declared with confidence: Break the Limits. Unlock the Possibilities. Let me give you some examples. Think about it. Until around twenty years ago, poverty in our country was considered a permanent problem. Five decades ago, slogans about removing poverty were raised from the Red Fort. But whenever anything had to be done at the policy level after that, the entire system would simply prepare files and sit on them.
Friends,
That happened because everyone believed that poverty could never be removed. “The population is too large, things will always remain like this.” Nobody even showed the courage to implement the right policies for eliminating poverty.
Friends,
When we came to government, the situation was still the same. I said from the Red Fort that I would build toilets for the poor. People in Parliament made fun of it. They said, “What kind of Prime Minister is this, speaking about building toilets from the Red Fort?” Such people could not understand how important a toilet is for a poor family, for poor mothers and sisters. Because of such thinking, the entire country remained deprived of many basic facilities. During the last 12 years, we changed this mindset. We empowered the poor. Power to Empower has been the guiding principle of my life. We empowered them. We launched schemes for their ease of living. And today the country can see the results. You must have read or heard about the recent World Bank report. The World Bank has said that within just 12–13 years, 50 crore people in India have come out of poverty.
Friends,
This is not a small change. It is the result of a mindset that says: Break the Limits.
Friends,
Let me give you another example. When I launched the semiconductor mission, many questions were raised. “Why do we need this mission now? Other countries are already making semiconductors. Semiconductors have been made around the world for the past 50 years. What will we gain by manufacturing semiconductors now?” This is the limitation of thinking.
Friends,
You may be surprised to know that fifty years ago a company had come to India to manufacture semiconductors. But it was effectively shown the red flag and sent back. I know nobody is going to clap for that. That was the work of those waving red flags. And when I spoke about the semiconductor mission, people again said that it was already too late.
Friends,
But I was determined. I said, “Even if it is late, should India continue sitting idle?” We began. I personally worked with officials to prepare plans. And today, within just four years, many semiconductor facilities have been established in the country. India has begun exporting chips. Many of your alumni are running and leading these facilities. They are providing leadership and execution. And believe me, there are opportunities everywhere for you. From chips to ships, everything will be made here, and it will be done by young people like you. But just imagine, if we had accepted the idea that others were already doing it and we should not even try, none of this would have happened.
Friends,
Let me give another strong example, the space sector. Earlier, we had a limited platform in ISRO, where entry itself was highly restricted. Any launch or new mission had to go through a rigid system. Young people outside ISRO did not even get opportunities. I told the ministry that our young innovators must get a chance in this sector. We opened India’s space sector to India’s youth. And today, look at what has happened. An alumnus of IIT Kharagpur, Pawan, through Skyroot Aerospace, gave India the distinction of launching its first private rocket. Today many such space startups are taking India’s space programme forward at a new pace. Once these things seemed impossible. Today they are possible. Today they are reality. And I can proudly say that your alumni have made a major contribution in turning the impossible into the possible.
Friends,
The country has high expectations from all of you. The next two decades will be among the most productive years of your lives. By 2047, many of you will be in leadership positions. These years will also be the most decisive years for India’s development. Therefore, every success of yours will be important for the nation. You must always ask yourselves: which challenge before the country would you like to help solve? Remember my mantra, friends: Nation First. When you move forward with this mindset, it will certainly create new opportunities for you and bring great benefits to the country as well.
Friends,
You have done outstanding work over the past 75 years. Now you must move forward with the determination that when IIT Kharagpur celebrates its 100th year, it should do so in a Developed India. In the years 1925–27, the freedom fighters imprisoned on this very land took a pledge that they would achieve independence, and within twenty years they did. Today, let us take a pledge from this same place that within twenty years we will build a Developed India. We will do it. And for this, we will devote ourselves completely and work tirelessly. And since I am on the soil of Bengal today, I will conclude with the words of Swami Vivekananda: Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached. Once again, on this special occasion, I extend my heartfelt best wishes to all of you.
Thank you very much.
Namaskar.

title: WOMEN’S LEADERSHIP, INNOVATION AND COLLECTIVE ACTION CAN SHAPE SOLUTIONS TO GLOBAL CHALLENGES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
subtitle:
BRICS is not a challenge to any country, it is for shared prosperity and well-being of all nations: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

TECHNOLOGICAL ADVANCEMENT MUST BE GUIDED BY HUMAN-CENTRED APPROACH, ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS, COMPASSION, AND ACCOUNTABILITY:  LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER STRESSES STRONGER BRICS COLLABORATION TO TACKLE CLIMATE CHANGE, TERRORISM, CYBERCRIME AND DRUG TRAFFICKING

WE MUST MOVE BEYOND ‘WOMEN EMPOWERMENT’ TO REALIZE ‘WOMEN-LED DEVELOPMENT’: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER ADDRESSES THE INAUGURAL CEREMONY OF THE BRICS WOMEN LEADERS SUMMIT AT BANASTHALI VIDYAPITH
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 NOV 2026 3:11PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today called upon women leaders from BRICS countries to harness their collective leadership, experience, and innovative capabilities to address global challenges and shape a more peaceful, stable, and prosperous world. Addressing the inaugural ceremony of the BRICS Women Leaders Summit as the Chief Guest at Banasthali Vidyapith, Tonk (Rajasthan), he said that women’s confidence, positive outlook, and capacity for innovation could open new pathways for resolving complex issues confronting nations and humanity.
Emphasising the importance of cooperation among BRICS nations, Shri Birla observed that despite differences in geographical, economic, and political circumstances, countries share several common challenges that require collective responses. He underlined that global peace and stability are essential prerequisites for economic and social progress, noting that unrest in one country can have far-reaching consequences across the world. He added that BRICS provides a vital platform for dialogue, cooperation, and the sharing of ideas and best practices, enabling countries to work towards shared interests and common solutions.
Highlighting the transformative potential of technology, particularly Artificial Intelligence, Lok Sabha Speaker called for its responsible application across sectors such as healthcare, education, agriculture, defence, cybersecurity, and women’s entrepreneurship. He stressed that technological advancement must be guided by a human-centred approach, ethical considerations, compassion, and accountability. Ensuring that AI serves humanity and makes the lives of ordinary citizens safer and better, he said, must remain a shared responsibility.
Shri Birla also emphasised the need to strengthen collaboration in addressing threats such as climate change, terrorism, cybercrime, and drug trafficking. He noted that sharing innovations, experiences, and successful practices across countries could generate fresh perspectives and enable BRICS nations to respond more effectively to emerging global concerns.
Referring to India’s vision of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’—the world is one family—Shri Birla said that BRICS is not a challenge to any country, nor is its purpose to challenge anyone. Rather, its guiding philosophy is rooted in the shared prosperity and well-being of all nations. He reiterated that India’s outlook extends beyond BRICS, with every country holding importance in the pursuit of global welfare and cooperation.
Highlighting India’s efforts towards women’s empowerment, Shri Birla referred to initiatives such as Self-Help Groups, Lakhpati Didi, and Drone Didi, which are creating opportunities for women to become economically independent and self-reliant. He noted that women are also playing a crucial role in financial inclusion and in driving socio-economic transformation. He further emphasised that the Constitution of India guarantees equality to every individual and that women in India have enjoyed the right to vote since the Constitution came into force. He said that the Government continues to work towards ensuring equal opportunities, dignity, safety, and privacy for women.
Shri Birla said that the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam represents a historic and far-reaching initiative towards strengthening women’s political participation from Panchayats to Parliament. Underscoring the imperative of ensuring equal access for women to education, technology, digital services, and financial resources, he called for moving beyond ‘Women Empowerment’ to realize the vision of ‘Women-led Development’—so that women do not remain mere participants in development, but play a decisive role in shaping its direction.
Lok Sabha Speaker lauded the legacy of Banasthali Vidyapith, recalling how an institution that began with just five students has grown into a distinguished centre of women’s education with around 18,000 students today. He paid tribute to its founders, Pandit Hiralal Shastri and Smt. Ratan Shastri, whose vision was inspired by the ideals of Mahatma Gandhi, the freedom movement, and the spirit of nation-building. He noted that students of the institution receive training across diverse fields—including technology, aviation, and equestrian activities—and have gone on to assume leadership roles in the Armed Forces, science, and other key sectors.
He expressed confidence that the Summit would provide a meaningful platform for women leaders from BRICS countries to exchange experiences, share best practices, and forge lasting partnerships. He hoped that the fresh ideas, innovations, and experiences shared at Banasthali Vidyapith would inspire BRICS nations to work together for the welfare of humanity, ensuring that women are not merely participants in the process of change, but among its leading architects.
Being held from 21 to 23 November 2026, the BRICS Women Leaders Summit serves as a premier international forum for deliberations on critical themes including women’s leadership, political participation, capacity building, digital security, and cyber safety. The Summit aims to foster new avenues of cooperation to advance women’s empowerment and leadership by sharing experiences and best practices across nations. Women parliamentarians, policymakers, academicians, entrepreneurs, and other distinguished delegates from BRICS and partner countries are participating in the Summit.

मुझे विश्वास है कि विभिन्न देशों की महिला नेतृत्वकर्ताओं के बीच यह संवाद सहयोग और साझा संकल्पों को नई दिशा देगा।

title: ITRA, Jamnagar Organises Three National CME Programmes, Bringing Together 90 Ayurveda Faculty Members from 13 States
subtitle:
Six-Day Programmes Focus on Strengthening Diagnostic Competencies, Clinical Skills and Teaching Capabilities

Around 45 Experts from Reputed Institutions Participate as Resource Persons
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 NOV 2026 6:19PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, an Institution of National Importance under the Ministry of Ayush, organised three simultaneous six-day National Continuing Medical Education (CME) programmes from 16 to 21 November 2026. Conducted by the Departments of Kriya Sharir, Roganidan and Vikriti Vigyan, and Prasuti Tantra and Streeroga, the programmes brought together 90 Ayurveda faculty members from 13 states. Around 45 eminent academicians, clinicians and healthcare experts from reputed institutions participated as resource persons.=
The programmes were conducted under the leadership of Prof. (Dr.) Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA, with the objective of strengthening subject-specific knowledge, diagnostic competencies, clinical skills and teaching capabilities of Ayurveda faculty members. They also focused on integrating classical Ayurvedic principles with contemporary medical knowledge and diagnostic methodologies.
At the inaugural session, Prof. (Dr.) Tanuja Nesari emphasised the importance of continuous professional development, scientific understanding of diagnostic methodologies and the integration of contemporary medical knowledge with the classical foundations of Ayurveda. Resource persons contributed through expert lectures, interactive discussions and practical sessions, facilitating interdisciplinary learning and exchange of academic and clinical experiences.
The CME chairpersons, including Prof. Shilpa Donga, Prof. Darshana Pandya and Dr. Swati Khandale, highlighted the importance of patient-centred healthcare, accurate diagnosis, clinical reasoning, evidence-based research and contemporary teaching methodologies in improving Ayurveda education and clinical services.
CME by the Department of Kriya Sharir
The CME organised by the Department of Kriya Sharir focused on strengthening the understanding of human physiology through classical Ayurvedic perspectives and contemporary scientific developments. The sessions explored the integration of traditional Ayurvedic concepts with modern physiological knowledge to enhance teaching and clinical understanding.
CME by the Department of Roganidan and Vikriti Vigyan: ‘MADHAV MIMAMSA-2026’
The Department of Roganidan and Vikriti Vigyan organised its CME under the title ‘MADHAV MIMAMSA-2026’, focusing on strengthening diagnostic competencies through the integration of classical Ayurvedic diagnostic principles with contemporary medical techniques.
The six-day programme covered subjects such as Nadi Pariksha, modern teaching methodologies, clinical diagnosis, advanced laboratory investigations, electrocardiography (ECG), computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The sessions highlighted systematic clinical assessment and the appropriate use of diagnostic investigations in disease evaluation.
CME by the Department of Prasuti Tantra and Streeroga
The Department of Prasuti Tantra and Streeroga conducted a six-day CME for teachers, covering key developments in obstetrics and gynaecology and their integration with classical Ayurvedic principles.
The academic sessions addressed Garbhini Paricharya, high-risk pregnancy, infertility and assisted reproductive techniques (ART), recurrent pregnancy loss, obstetric emergencies, puerperal care, contraception, breast diseases, congenital anomalies and gynaecological disorders.
Practical training and demonstrations included episiotomy and suturing techniques, colposcopy, Pap smear, vaginal smear, culture techniques and antenatal ultrasonography. The role of Panchakarma procedures in Stree Roga and Vandhyatva was also discussed in the context of integrative women's healthcare.
The three CME programmes provided a national platform for professional development, interdisciplinary knowledge exchange and capacity building among Ayurveda faculty members. The initiative reinforced the importance of diagnostic accuracy, clinical competence, research orientation and contemporary teaching methodologies in strengthening Ayurveda education and healthcare delivery.
The programmes reflect ITRA, Jamnagar's continued commitment to advancing Ayurveda education, research and clinical practice through faculty development and the integration of classical knowledge with contemporary scientific approaches.

title: Minister of State for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Shri Bhagirath Choudhary attends Bharat Food & Agro @ 2047 Conclave
subtitle: Shri Choudhary emphasizes on Balanced Use of Pesticides and Chemical fertilizers, Residue-Free Production, Climate-Resilient Farming and Value Addition through Food Processing
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 NOV 2026 5:02PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shri Bhagirath Choudhary today attended the National conclave ‘Bharat Food & Agro @ 2047’, organised on the theme ‘Growth, Innovation, Global Reach’
at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
Addressing the conclave, Shri Bhagirath Choudhary emphasised that farmers are at the centre of India’s economic progress and that a strong and resilient agricultural sector is vital for achieving the vision of a developed India. He said that the focus must extend beyond increasing agricultural production to improving quality, ensuring food safety, promoting sustainable practices and strengthening farmers' incomes.
The Minister also highlighted the importance of balanced use of pesticides and chemical fertilisers, residue-free agricultural production, climate-resilient farming, indigenous alternatives to imported agricultural products and value addition through food processing. He also called for greater adoption of natural farming, urging farmers to begin with at least 10 per cent of their cultivated area and gradually expand based on their experience.
The Minister also highlighted the potential of Shree Anna (millets), including jowar and bajra, and called for greater research, processing and development of new food products to expand their domestic and international markets. He stressed the need to strengthen farmer-producer organisations (FPOs), MSMEs and linkages between farmers and food processing industries.
Referring to government initiatives, he highlighted the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund, Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme and One District One Product (ODOP) initiative. He encouraged entrepreneurs to leverage these initiatives, adopt modern technologies, artificial intelligence and smart packaging, and connect local products with global markets.
The conclave also provided a platform for entrepreneurs, industry representatives, scientists and policymakers to exchange experiences, discuss challenges and explore opportunities for collaboration. The discussions focused on strengthening the food processing sector, improving product quality, promoting innovation, enhancing export capabilities and ensuring that the benefits of agricultural value addition reach farmers.

title: Sixth Round of India–Canada CEPA Negotiations Concludes in New Delhi
subtitle:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and Canadian Minister Maninder Sidhu Reaffirm Commitment to a Balanced and Mutually Beneficial CEPA

Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal and Canadian Vice Minister Mr. Glenn Purves review status of talks
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 NOV 2026 8:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The sixth round of negotiations for the India-Canada Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) was held in New Delhi from 11 to 20 November 2026. The Indian delegation was led by Dr. Brij Mohan Mishra, Chief Negotiator, while the Canadian delegation was led by Ms. Mary-Catherine Speirs, Chief Negotiator. The negotiations covered key areas, including Trade in goods, Trade in services, Rules of origin, Trade Remedies, Intellectual Property and Investment promotion.
The negotiating round opened with a warm and constructive meeting in New Delhi on 11 November between Shri Piyush Goyal, Minister of Commerce and Industry and Mr. Maninder Sidhu, Canada’s Minister of International Trade. Both Ministers underscored the importance of a balanced and mutually beneficial CEPA that delivers meaningful market access, builds on the complementarities of both economies and creates new opportunities for trade and investment.
